# River towns vote to share one flood warning system

Four councils along the lower Ashwater voted on Thursday to run a single flood warning system, ending years in which each town bought and maintained its own river gauges, sirens and text-message alerts.

The plan pools 38 water-level sensors into one network and gives every resident in the four towns the same alert, at the same time, whichever side of a council boundary they live on.

"Last spring the water did not stop at the town sign, and our warnings should not either," said Hollins Ford councillor Dara Venn, who proposed the scheme.

## What changes for residents

From June, alerts will come from one number and one app. Residents who already signed up with their own town will be moved over automatically, the councils said.

- Sirens will sound in all four towns when any gauge passes the red line.
- Text alerts will include the expected peak time and level.
- A public map will show every sensor's reading, updated every five minutes.

The joint system will cost about 410,000 euros over five years, less than the four councils currently spend between them, according to a report presented at the meeting.

Not everyone was convinced. Two councillors in Lower Marsh voted against, arguing that the town would lose control over when its own sirens sound.
